links.targetTitle: Spark instances go live before the RRC Framework is fully im

title: Each Instance declares whether its risk capital rests on a fully implemented or a pending risk model
content:
A.6.1.1.1.2.6.1.3 introduces a status carried by every Active Instance: "The `RRC Framework Full Implementation` status defines whether the Instance Financial RRC is calculated based on a fully implemented risk model ... or a pending risk model. If the Instance Financial RRC is calculated based on a fully implemented risk model the status is `Covered`. If ... a pending risk model the status is `Pending`."

This attaches an explicit epistemic label to a risk number. The Required Risk Capital figure for an exposure is an output of a model, and the flag says whether that model is finished. The SparkLend USDS Instance, for example, is marked `Covered` (A.6.1.1.1.2.6.1.3.1.1.1.1).

The reason this is more than bookkeeping: risk capital requirements aggregate. A portfolio-level capital figure computed partly from finished models and partly from provisional ones is not uniformly trustworthy, and without per-instance labelling the aggregate would hide which parts are soft. Marking each Instance lets a reader — or the Risk Council — see how much of Spark's stated capital adequacy rests on models still being built.

The wider methodological point generalizes well beyond Sky: a framework that computes numbers from models should record the maturity of each model alongside the number. Declaring uncertainty at the level where it originates is what keeps an aggregate honest, and it creates a natural work queue — every `Pending` is a known gap with a named owner.
description: The RRC Framework Full Implementation flag is Covered when the Instance Financial RRC comes from a fully implemented risk model and Pending when the model is still provisional.
